correctness.rationale: Reconstructed incidence unit Schur elimination, nilpotent-radical necessity, explicit invertible generalized inverse, independent strict-entry count, and square-zero comparison for arbitrary posets and all characteristics. The exact weight ratio gives a central phase theta kernel; uniform discrete-Gaussian tails and bounded sum of second-order errors give O_q(1/log n). Independent witness linear systems and Schur counts were exhaustively checked on 22,156 incidence elements; 97,829 square-zero elements checked, including F4; 12 numerical finite-size theta approximations. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove limits.

originality.rationale: Prior general factorization of regular incidence elements (Khripchenko-Novikov, Theorem 4) and the q=2 chain total (OEIS A079491) are explicitly excluded from novelty. Assessed claim is the exact matching support-strata count for every finite poset in two generally nonisomorphic algebras together with the fixed-q theta full law, quantitative total-variation rate, and relative normalizer for growing chains. Exact statement/implication searches did not find a dominating result in inspected sources; residual unindexed asymptotic work is documented.
residual_risks: Related q-deformed binomial asymptotics could contain an equivalent theta-limit theorem without reference to incidence algebras.
Later sections of Gould-Johnson-Naz and other unindexed monoid literature were not exhaustively inspected; no full historical uniqueness guarantee.
Khripchenko-Novikov qualitatively covers regular incidence normal forms, so no novelty is attached to that sublemma or its straightforward consequences.

value.rationale: The natural von Neumann regular locus in finite incidence monoids is compared exactly across arbitrarily different radical multiplication structures and every prescribed diagonal-zero set, yielding a whole family of invariants rather than isolated examples. The growing triangular-monoid law sharpens prior binary totals and loglog modal estimates to an explicit non-Gaussian phase-sensitive full local distribution and normalization with a rate. It is motivated by a natural randomly sampled semigroup element rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. Prior exact binary counts and qualitative regularity classifications are acknowledged as known, not presented as contributions.
